sections.html:
In Wausau the quickest closings come from buyers who do not rely on a mortgage, since loan approval and appraisal are the steps that stretch a listing. The alternatives are hiring an agent or selling the house yourself. Every path finishes with the same three items: a condition report handed to the buyer, an electronic transfer return, and a deed recorded at the Marathon County Register of Deeds.

Wausau is the Marathon County seat, on the Wisconsin River in central Wisconsin. The 2025 population estimate is 40,188, up 0.5 percent from the 39,994 counted in 2020. The river divides the city into east and west sides, with numbered streets on the east and numbered avenues on the west, which helps when you describe a location to an out-of-town buyer.

Wausau homes cost well under Milwaukee-area suburban prices. The median owner-occupied value is $167,900 for 2020 to 2024, and 57.6 percent of housing units are owner-occupied.

sections.h2: What Wisconsin requires of a Wausau seller
sections.html:
A home with one to four dwelling units comes with a seller duty: give the buyer a completed real estate condition report no later than 10 days after the contract is accepted. Chapter 709 of the Wisconsin Statutes lets a buyer who never receives it rescind within two business days after the 10 days run out and recover any deposit. Personal representatives, trustees and court-appointed fiduciaries who never occupied the home need not complete the form.

The grantor also owes a transfer fee of 30 cents per $100 of value under s. 77.22, which is $3 per $1,000, collected when the deed is recorded. Grantor and grantee both sign the electronic return. Transfers by will, descent or survivorship are among those exempted by s. 77.25.

sections.h2: How property taxes and assessments work in Wausau
sections.html:
You can pay Wausau taxes in full by January 31 or split them into installments due January 31, April 30 and July 31. Special assessment charges on the bill are due in full by January 31. The city clerk's office takes these payments, and Marathon County does not accept payments for the City of Wausau.

Ways to pay include ePayments, ACH, participating banks until July 31, the drop boxes at City Hall on Grant Street or across from the post office on Forest Street, the mail, or the counter at 407 Grant Street between 8:00 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. A returned electronic payment carries a $45 fee.

The Assessment Department, at 715-261-6600, values property under chapter 70 of the Wisconsin Statutes at the full value obtainable in a private sale. The city's last revaluation was as of January 1, 2020, and the state checks assessments against sales to see whether the citywide ratio stays between 90 and 110 percent of market value. A mailed notice tells you when your assessment changes, and the Open Book period lets you meet an appraiser before any formal appeal.

Marathon County lists a 5x5 short-term loan of up to $5,000 for taxes that are three years or more past due. It is open to applicants who are 55 or older or disabled, and it carries a $3 monthly service charge. Call the county at 715-261-1150 to ask about eligibility.

Whatever you owe, get a payoff figure before you accept an offer, and let the title company pay it from your proceeds at closing.

sections.h2: Which Wausau city rules matter before I list?
sections.html:
Property maintenance and rental rules are the two areas most likely to affect a sale. The Inspections and Zoning division, at 407 Grant Street and 715-261-6780, handles complaints and permits. Its rules cover trash containers, parked vehicles and yard signs, and a buyer's agent walking the property will notice any violation.

  • Trash and recycling carts may go out no sooner than 3:00 p.m. the day before pickup and must be removed by 11:00 a.m. the day after. Between pickups they belong in a garage, shed, or behind or beside the house.
  • Vehicles may be parked only on hard-surfaced driveway areas, not on the grass. Inoperative or unlicensed vehicles are not allowed on residential lots.
  • Boats, trailers, campers and similar equipment cannot sit in a required front yard or corner side yard except on a hard-surfaced driveway, and anything over 30 feet must be in an enclosed structure.
  • Zoning allows two yard signs at a time, each no larger than 6 square feet and 4 feet high. Real estate signs cannot be placed on boulevards, public right-of-way or utility poles.

If the house is a rental, the division's rental properties page lists rental registration, rental licensing and inspection, and a rent abatement program. Ask which of those apply to your unit before you transfer it.

sections.h2: Recording the deed in Marathon County
sections.html:
Mail the original deed, the electronic transfer return receipt and the recording fee to the Register of Deeds at 500 Forest Street, Wausau. The fee is $30 per document, and any transfer fee is paid at the same time. Since January 1, 2026 the office returns recorded documents electronically unless you include a self-addressed, stamped envelope, so write your email address on the submission.

The county cannot give legal advice, so a title company or an attorney commonly prepares the deed. The recorded-document certification fee is $1 and copies cost $2 for the first page and $1 for each additional page.

Write down the timing and the net cash for each route.

  • Agent listing. Reaches the most buyers if the house shows well and you can wait for financing.
  • Selling on your own. Keeps more of the price but puts disclosures, signs and the contract on you.
  • Cash offer. Fits an inherited house, a rental with tenants, deferred repairs or a short clock. Get the number in writing, and find out who pays title and recording costs.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Wausau?
faqs.a: The Marathon County Register of Deeds charges $30 per document, plus any real estate transfer fee shown on the electronic return receipt. Copies are $2 for the first page and $1 for each additional page. Documents go to 500 Forest Street, Wausau.

faqs.q: When are Wausau property taxes due?
faqs.a: Pay in full by January 31, or in installments due January 31, April 30 and July 31. Special assessment charges on the bill must be paid in full by January 31. The City of Wausau collects these payments, not Marathon County.

faqs.q: Do I have to give a buyer a condition report in Wausau?
faqs.a: Yes, for one-to-four unit homes. Wis. Stat. chapter 709 requires the completed report within 10 days after the contract is accepted. A buyer who does not get it may rescind within two business days after that period, unless you are an exempt fiduciary who never lived in the home.

faqs.q: Can I put a for-sale sign in my Wausau yard?
faqs.a: Yes, on your own property. Zoning allows two yard signs at one time, each up to 6 square feet and 4 feet tall. Signs cannot be placed on boulevards, other public right-of-way or utility poles.

faqs.q: What is the Wisconsin transfer fee on a Wausau sale?
faqs.a: The grantor pays 30 cents per $100 of value, which is $3 per $1,000, when the deed is recorded. Transfers by will, descent or survivorship are exempt under s. 77.25.
